label: Free 2.0
title: One handler, eight legal areas
lede: Inverse 2.0 knows the legal area of every declaration. Germany, Austria, Switzerland, France, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands and Poland are built in, and each record shows which state of the rules it followed.

items.title: Pick the legal area per shop or per request
items.text: Set a default jurisdiction and allow a list of others, so a shop that sells in several countries gets the right language and the right legal status on every record.
items.outputTitle: Real run: a request for fr is accepted, one for pl (not allowed) falls back to de

items.title: See how well each country is covered
items.text: The CLI prints the legal status of one area, its sources and what changed. France, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands and Poland say plainly that they rest on the directive only.
items.output:
France (fr): directive only, national act not read
The French implementing act was not read. Check the Code de la consommation on legifrance.gouv.fr.

Legal status checked on 2026-10-12

Sources:
  - Directive (EU) 2023/2673, Article 11a Consumer Rights Directive (withdrawal function)
  - National implementing act not read

Changes:
  2026-10-12  2.0.0  Legal status is kept per legal area (`legalRevisions`, `getLegalRevision`). France, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands and Poland added on the basis of the directive only. No change in requirements.
  ...

items.title: Let CI notice a legal change
items.text: With --since the command exits 1 when the library has a newer legal status than your last review, so a cron or CI job can remind you.
items.code: npx inverse legal --jurisdiction de --since 2026-10-01   # exit 1 if something is newer
items.output:
$ npx inverse legal --jurisdiction de --since 2026-10-01
Germany (de): national provision checked
Both duties apply to online contracts with consumers.

Changes since 2026-10-01 (checked 2026-10-12):
  2026-10-12  2.0.0  Legal status is kept per legal area (`legalRevisions`, `getLegalRevision`). ...
  ...
exit code 1

$ npx inverse legal --jurisdiction de --since 2030-01-01
Germany (de): national provision checked
Both duties apply to online contracts with consumers.

Nothing new since 2030-01-01.
exit code 0

items.title: Read the legal status from code
items.text: The single legalRevision export became getLegalRevision per area. Use the checked date in your own compliance docs or to fail a build.

note: France, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands and Poland follow Article 11a of the directive only; the national laws were not read and the texts are not reviewed by a lawyer or native speaker. 2.0 also needs Node 22.
